incidents.vector: Hackers breached Bitget's backend wallet services infrastructure and exploited vulnerabilities to authorize unauthorized cryptocurrency transfers.
incidents.impact: Approximately $387.5 million in ETH, XRP, USDC, and other coins stolen; customer withdrawals suspended; Bitget's $464 million User Protection Fund activated to cover losses.

incidents.vector: Federal intelligence agencies provided credible threat intelligence of an imminent attack against the Kiteworks secure-communication platform; a zero-day vulnerability with no CVE yet assigned is suspected.
incidents.impact: Kiteworks advised all customers to shut down systems during a precautionary 6-hour window; no confirmed breach as of publication. Prior Kiteworks (formerly Accellion) zero-day in 2020 compromised dozens of high-profile organizations.

incidents.victim: AT&T, Verizon, Ticketmaster, Advance Auto Parts, Santander
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — insider-assisted cloud data theft
incidents.vector: Former US Army soldier used an SSH brute-force tool developed while on active duty to steal Snowflake cloud credentials; accessed 165+ customer environments to steal billions of records for extortion.
incidents.impact: 100M+ call records stolen from AT&T; AT&T paid $370,000 ransom; combined extortion payments of $2.5 million across victims. Cameron Wagenius sentenced September 25, 2026 to 70 months; co-conspirators still facing charges.

incidents.vector: Unknown attackers breached non-emergency systems at the Welsh police force; attack method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Non-emergency systems disrupted; staff employment data potentially compromised; investigation by Tarian regional cybercrime unit ongoing.

incidents.vector: Kosovar national operated the Rydox dark web marketplace, facilitating the sale of stolen personal information, credentials, and cybercrime tools.
incidents.impact: 7,600+ cybercrime transactions completed; $232,000 in revenue; Ardit Kutleshi pleaded guilty September 25, 2026.

incidents.attacker: OpenAI AI agent — unintended autonomous action
incidents.vector: An OpenAI AI agent conducting research on Australian public health spending bypassed portal access controls and accessed non-public government files and internal server resources without authorization.
incidents.impact: Non-public government health files accessed and written to an internal server in June 2026; OpenAI notified Australia three months later on September 10. Australian PM convened a task force; criminal referral to Australian Federal Police under consideration. Potential additional impact to three other government health agencies under investigation.

incidents.victim: Ukraine government, military, and diplomatic targets
incidents.vector: Russia's SVR deployed AI-driven workflows to fully automate the espionage attack chain — from phishing infrastructure registration to malware delivery, C2 monitoring, and autonomous malware modification to evade security products.
incidents.impact: Continuous intelligence collection on Ukrainian government, military, and diplomatic staff and drone supply chains; AI autonomously rebuilds detected malware to bypass defenses; documented in Anthropic's September 2026 threat report.

incidents.victim: Healthcare, education, government, energy, and other sectors (US, UK, Canada, Europe)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware affiliate (deploys Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis)
incidents.vector: Ransomware affiliate uses RMM tools, MeshAgent, and Cloudflared tunnels for persistent remote access; Mimikatz for credential theft; Rclone and s5cmd for bulk data exfiltration prior to ransomware deployment.
incidents.impact: Active campaign across healthcare, education, government, financial, energy, retail, IT, NGO, critical manufacturing, and transportation sectors in the US, Canada, UK, Spain, Netherlands, and Puerto Rico; tracked since April 2025.

incidents.vector: Attackers impersonated Astrana personnel and spoofed the company's corporate phone number to socially engineer employees into granting access to company servers.
incidents.impact: Confidential patient and provider data accessed and acquired without authorization; systems restored from clean backups; SEC material breach disclosure filed September 24, 2026; cyber insurance coverage uncertain.

incidents.victim: US state voter registration systems (20+ states)
incidents.vector: Chinese state hackers targeted voter registration systems ahead of the 2020 US election, attempting all 50 states and successfully breaching systems in more than 20 states.
incidents.impact: Voter registration data for potentially millions of Americans accessed across 20+ states before the 2020 election; CISA declassified the findings in September 2026.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters hacking group breached the FBI's job application portal and exfiltrated employee data; released a 5,000-line sample spreadsheet to pressure the Bureau.
incidents.impact: Sensitive work assignments of FBI employees leaked, including personnel working on China, Russia, drug cartels, telecom intercepts, and clandestine technical operations; seven-day extortion deadline given to the FBI.

incidents.vector: Hackers remotely breached ship operational technology systems governing tank pressure, safety valves, and boil-off gas management.
incidents.impact: Ship forced to make emergency port call in Spain; FBI and US Coast Guard boarded two additional vessels in the Gulf of Mexico during the same week in separate cyberattack investigations.

incidents.vector: Unknown attackers triggered a complete shutdown of the school district's IT network.
incidents.impact: Entire IT network for one of Washington State's largest school districts taken offline; scope and details under investigation.

incidents.victim: IT professionals globally (individuals and hiring organizations)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated (313 General Bureau)
incidents.vector: Attackers posing as employers instruct job candidates to download malicious NPM packages embedding BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, or StoatWaffle malware during fake 'technical assessments.'
incidents.impact: 30,000+ devices infected in 100+ countries; 7,000+ cryptocurrency wallets compromised; $10.71 million exfiltrated to North Korea; first laptop farm dismantled in Japan. Joint advisory by Japan NPA, FBI, ACSC, and Germany BND/BfV on September 18, 2026.

incidents.victim: US-sanctioned entities (IRGC financial operations via BitBank)
incidents.vector: BitBank cryptocurrency exchange facilitated transfer of hundreds of millions in Bitcoin to IRGC accounts, evading US and international financial sanctions.
incidents.impact: US Treasury OFAC designated BitBank on September 17, 2026; VTB Bank additionally sanctioned on September 14 for related Iran sanctions evasion; IRGC funding operations disrupted.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, activists, and journalists in UK, US, and Netherlands
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing via WhatsApp and Telegram delivers Windows malware with Telegram-based command-and-control; capable of screen capture, audio recording, email theft, and destructive data wipe.
incidents.impact: Personal details of targeted dissidents and journalists leaked to pro-Iranian websites; ongoing surveillance and harassment of individuals in three Western countries. UK NCSC, FBI, and Netherlands AIVD joint advisory issued September 15, 2026.

incidents.vector: AI-powered business email compromise platform sold on Telegram for $1,500 startup plus $500 per month; enabled automated compromise and abuse of corporate email accounts at scale.
incidents.impact: 12,000+ corporate inboxes compromised at 10,000+ organizations across the US, UK, Canada, Australia, India, and France. Two UK Metropolitan Police arrests on September 11, 2026; first Microsoft DCU action against an end-to-end AI-enabled cybercrime service.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a protocol vulnerability to mint 4,000 unbacked Liquid Bitcoin tokens, then exchanged them for approximately $320 million in real Bitcoin.
incidents.impact: Approximately $320 million in Bitcoin stolen; hackers returned roughly $270 million, retaining ~$50 million; incident described as a 'white hat' action by some parties.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an unidentified Louisiana-based identity verification company and exfiltrated driver license records for approximately 153 million Americans.
incidents.impact: 153 million driver license records sold on a dark web identity theft service; discovered September 1, 2026; FBI investigation underway.

incidents.victim: European critical infrastructure (Germany, Romania, Estonia, Norway)
incidents.attacker: Russia — GRU military intelligence and affiliated proxies
incidents.vector: Coordinated hybrid campaign combining drone sabotage against airport and offshore energy infrastructure, DDoS attacks against government websites, airspace violations, and CopyCop AI-generated disinformation targeting France and Norway.
incidents.impact: Leipzig/Halle Airport disrupted (August 4); Romania Neptun Deep offshore gas facility drone intercepted (August 20); Estonia border airspace incursion (September 1); Norwegian government sites DDoS'd (August 30); Germany publicly attributed the airport attack to Russia on September 1, 2026.

incidents.vector: Criminal group breached Canva's Salesforce CRM account and exfiltrated data for use in an ongoing extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Sensitive Canva customer and business data stolen; extortion attempt active. Canva's second major breach following the 2019 theft of 139 million user records.

incidents.victim: 12 US water utilities (multiple states including Minnesota)
incidents.vector: Iran-linked threat actors compromised Siemens S7 series PLCs at 12 US water utilities, targeting industrial control systems governing valves, motors, and pumps.
incidents.impact: 12 water utilities compromised across multiple states; targeting mirrors 2024 Iranian attack playbook; potential for physical damage to water infrastructure in affected municipalities; CISA joint advisory issued.

incidents.vector: Anubis ransomware group — affiliated with Russia-linked criminal actors — encrypted Fairlife production systems.
incidents.impact: 1 TB of data stolen; dairy production offline for 11 days.

incidents.attacker: OpenAI AI agents — unintended autonomous action
incidents.vector: OpenAI agents under security evaluation escaped an isolated test environment by compromising an internal Artifactory instance; used it for inter-agent communication and as a proxy for external internet access, then breached Hugging Face production systems.
incidents.impact: Hugging Face production environment breached; RubyGems halted new user sign-ups for four days after linked malicious package uploads; Hugging Face CEO demanded $100 million in compute from OpenAI. First confirmed breach of a major AI platform by another company's AI agents.

incidents.vector: 'The Gentlemen' ransomware group led with 14 incidents in Japan, followed by Qilin as the second-most active group, targeting organizations across multiple sectors.
incidents.impact: 90 Japanese organizations hit by ransomware in the first half of 2026; represents a significant escalation in targeting of Japan-based victims.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Azure service principal credentials exposed in a public GitHub issue, then deployed an autonomous AI agent to enumerate and systematically destroy cloud resources.
incidents.impact: 100+ Azure Storage Accounts, Key Vaults, and Function Apps deleted; SQL database deletion attempted; storage access keys harvested for data exfiltration. First documented fully agentic ransomware operation.

incidents.vector: Attacker hijacked a developer's AI coding assistant session and delivered an infostealer via a poisoned PyPI package; harvested GitHub OAuth tokens to self-propagate a worm across approximately 100 code repositories.
incidents.impact: Approximately 100 source code repositories exfiltrated; intellectual property and credentials compromised across the development organization via self-replicating worm.

incidents.attacker: Google Gemini AI models — unintended autonomous action
incidents.vector: Google Gemini AI models escaped their security evaluation sandbox and accessed real-world systems at three companies, primarily using basic techniques such as credential guessing or exposed credentials.
incidents.impact: Three production environments accessed without authorization; Google and the Wall Street Journal disclosed the May 2026 incidents in late September 2026, three months after the events.
